title: Past futures of the book
note: One record per speculation. Labels must match the codebook exactly; the site warns about any it does not recognise. v0.3: reach removed; spatial distance (Here, Elsewhere, Everywhere) is distance from the speaker; Speculative designer renamed Designer.

speculations.who: Charles W. Eliot (introduction to Keystone’s teachers’ guide)
speculations.text: The stereograph may be used advantageously either with or without a textbook.
speculations.speaker: Educator
speculations.source: Charles W. Eliot, General Introduction, in Keystone View Company, Visual Education: Teachers’ Guide to Keystone “600 Set” (Meadville, PA: Keystone View Company, 1906; digitised edition c.1922). Internet Archive.
speculations.verify: Guide copyrighted 1906–1922; confirm which edition carries this introduction.

speculations.text: The moving picture art will largely supplement the art of printing.
speculations.speaker: Inventor
speculations.source: Frank Parker Hulette, interview with Thomas Edison, Moving Picture World, 22 July 1911, pp. 104–105. Compiled in “Thomas Edison’s Education Predictions”, muninn.net.

speculations.text: Books will soon be obsolete in the public schools. … Our school system will be completely changed inside of ten years.
speculations.speaker: Inventor
speculations.source: Frederick James Smith, “The Evolution of the Motion Picture VI”, New York Dramatic Mirror 70, 9 July 1913, p. 24; cited in Cuban (1986).
speculations.verify: Second sentence confirmed in the compilation; check the first against the original page.

speculations.text: I believe that the motion picture is destined to revolutionize our educational system and that in a few years it will supplant largely, if not entirely, the use of textbooks.
speculations.speaker: Inventor
speculations.source: Hugh Weir, “The Story of the Motion Picture”, McClure’s 54, November 1922, p. 85; quoted in Cuban (1986).
speculations.verify: Full wording taken from secondary sources; check against McClure’s.

speculations.text: Textbooks as the principal medium of teaching will be as obsolete as the horse and carriage are now.
speculations.speaker: Inventor
speculations.source: Hugh Weir, “What Edison Would Like to Do with the Movies”, Collier’s 75, 21 February 1925, pp. 20–21. Compiled in muninn.net (as above).

speculations.who: Benjamin H. Darrow, Ohio School of the Air
speculations.text: The minds of boys and girls will be dipped directly into the flame of living genius.
speculations.speaker: Educator
speculations.source: Benjamin H. Darrow, first Ohio School of the Air conference, November 1929; quoted in Ohio History Connection, “‘The Flame of Living Genius’: The Ohio School of the Air”, Ohio Memory.

speculations.text: With a large-screen receiver in every room, programs can be fashioned to the needs of your children. … These programs will be able to tap the Nation’s finest teaching personnel and material.
speculations.speaker: Policymaker
speculations.source: “Federal Communications Commissioner Predicts Educational TV Will Become the Schoolhouse of the Air”, TV Guide, 18 June 1955. Media History Digital Library (Lantern).

speculations.text: The role of the teacher may well be changed, for machine instruction will affect several traditional practices.
speculations.speaker: Researcher
speculations.source: B. F. Skinner, “Teaching Machines”, Science 128(3330), 24 October 1958, pp. 969–977.

speculations.text: Television can extend the influence of the most talented teachers.
speculations.speaker: Company
speculations.source: “Television and the Crisis in Our Classrooms”, Electronic Age (RCA), Autumn 1959, pp. 3–5. World Radio History archive.

speculations.text: Educational television would not replace teachers but would increase their power to teach.
speculations.speaker: Policymaker
speculations.source: Edmund S. Muskie, Congressional Record – Senate, 12 September 1961. Muskie Archives, Bates College.

speculations.text: One can predict that in a few more years millions of schoolchildren will have access to what Philip of Macedon’s son Alexander enjoyed as a royal prerogative: the personal services of a tutor as well-informed and responsive as Aristotle.
speculations.speaker: Researcher
speculations.source: Patrick Suppes, “The Uses of Computers in Education”, Scientific American 215(3), September 1966, pp. 206–220.

speculations.text: I think the computer will blow up the school. … There won’t be schools in the future.
speculations.speaker: Researcher
speculations.source: Seymour Papert, 1984; quoted in Cuban (1986).

speculations.text: VR provides a route to success for children who might otherwise fail in our education system.
speculations.speaker: Researcher
speculations.source: William Winn, “A Conceptual Basis for Educational Applications of Virtual Reality”, Technical Report R-93-9, Human Interface Technology Laboratory, University of Washington, August 1993.

speculations.text: Fifty years from now, there will be only 10 institutions in the whole world that deliver higher education.
speculations.speaker: Company
speculations.source: Steven Leckart, “The Stanford Education Experiment Could Change Higher Learning Forever”, Wired, March 2012.
speculations.verify: Wording via secondary sources; check against the Wired article.

speculations.text: A host of struggling colleges and universities … will disappear or merge in the next 10 to 15 years.
speculations.speaker: Researcher
speculations.source: “Clayton Christensen: Bottom 25 Percent of Colleges Will Disappear”, EdSurge, 5 November 2013.

speculations.text: We’re at the cusp of using AI for probably the biggest positive transformation that education has ever seen.
speculations.speaker: Company
speculations.source: Sal Khan, “How AI Could Save (Not Destroy) Education”, TED, 2023; Khan Academy blog, 1 May 2023.

speculations.text: If you just took the next 18 months, the AIs will come in as a teacher’s aide and give feedback on writing. … The AIs will get to that ability, to be as good a tutor as any human ever could.
speculations.speaker: Company
speculations.source: Bill Gates, ASU+GSV Summit, San Diego, April 2023; reported in CNBC, 22 April 2023.

speculations.text: With AI, over the next decade, that will become free, commonplace — great medical advice, great tutoring.
speculations.speaker: Company
speculations.source: Bill Gates, The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, NBC, February 2025; reported by NBC/CNBC.

speculations.text: At school: books are fed into a hand-cranked machine, and their contents are transmitted through wires to the pupils’ heads.
speculations.speaker: Writer or artist
speculations.source: Villemard, “En l’an 2000” (school scene), French illustrated card, c.1910. Reproduced in Postcrossing Blog, “En l’an 2000”, 17 October 2013.
speculations.verify: Series dated c.1899–1910 in secondary sources; confirm the card’s date.

speculations.text: Today Tommy found a real book!
speculations.note: Set in 2157. Children are taught alone at home by mechanical teachers; a printed book found in an attic makes Margie long for the old schools and “the fun they had”. Often read as anticipating the computer; coded as the source names it.
speculations.speaker: Writer or artist
speculations.source: Isaac Asimov, “The Fun They Had”, Boys and Girls Page (newspaper supplement), 1 December 1951; collected in Earth Is Room Enough (1957).

speculations.text: The same infinite detail and awareness could be projected through radios and televisors, but are not.
speculations.note: Books are banned and burned; wall-sized televisions fill the home. Faber’s line insists the loss lies in use, not in the medium.
speculations.speaker: Writer or artist
speculations.source: Ray Bradbury, Fahrenheit 451 (New York: Ballantine, 1953).

speculations.text: A computer would send him back the names and addresses of all those who had inserted the same description.
speculations.note: Illich proposes replacing schools with “learning webs”, including computer-based peer matching.
speculations.speaker: Researcher
speculations.source: Ivan Illich, Deschooling Society (New York: Harper & Row, 1971).
speculations.verify: First edition year (1971) and publisher to confirm.

speculations.text: An interactive book, A Young Lady’s Illustrated Primer, raises and educates a girl, Nell, through stories that respond to her life, voiced by a remote human actor.
speculations.note: Set in the 22nd century. The tutor of the future takes the form of a book.
speculations.speaker: Writer or artist
speculations.source: Neal Stephenson, The Diamond Age: Or, a Young Lady’s Illustrated Primer (New York: Bantam Spectra, 1995).

speculations.text: …explore new ways of valuing teacher presence which are not resistant to the generative potential of automation.
speculations.note: A Twitter bot developed from teaching the Edinburgh MOOC ‘E-learning and digital cultures’, as a critical intervention in automated teaching.
speculations.speaker: Designer
speculations.source: Siân Bayne, “Teacherbot: Interventions in Automated Teaching”, Teaching in Higher Education, 2015. doi:10.1080/13562517.2015.1020783

speculations.text: Five vignettes of a fictional Australian high school, Lakeside, in 2030: growing dataveillance, digital deskilling of teachers, and the de-territorialisation of schooling.
speculations.note: The authors frame the vignettes as “social science fiction”, fiction used as a sociological research method, not as design fiction; coded Researcher accordingly.
speculations.speaker: Researcher
speculations.source: Neil Selwyn, Luci Pangrazio, Selena Nemorin and Carlo Perrotta, “What Might the School of 2030 Be Like? An Exercise in Social Science Fiction”, Learning, Media and Technology 45(1), 2020, pp. 90–106. doi:10.1080/17439884.2020.1694944

speculations.who: OECD, Back to the Future of Education
speculations.text: Scenario 4, ‘Learn-as-you-go’ (2040): school-based learning ends, and schooling as an institution disappears.
speculations.speaker: Policymaker
speculations.source: OECD, Back to the Future of Education: Four OECD Scenarios for Schooling (Paris: OECD Publishing, 2020).

speculations.text: A robot teacher, Ms. Brainmocker, runs the class at the Little Dipper School, handing out report tapes.
speculations.note: She malfunctions and praises a nonsense answer, and scolds a pupil for watching television on his wrist: “How many times have I told you, no TV in the classroom!”
speculations.speaker: Writer or artist
speculations.source: The Jetsons, “Elroy’s Mob”, ABC (Hanna-Barbera), first aired 17 March 1963; described in Matt Novak, “The Jetsons Get Schooled: Robot Teachers in the 21st Century Classroom”, Smithsonian Magazine (Paleofuture), 29 March 2013.
speculations.verify: Setting year (commonly given as 2062) not confirmed in the source used.

speculations.text: A professor prepares a lecture on Amazon deforestation with a talking software agent that finds articles and data, and brings a colleague into the lecture by video.
speculations.note: Concept video, premiered by John Sculley at the Educom higher-education conference; set, by inference, in September 2011.
speculations.speaker: Company
speculations.source: Apple Computer, Knowledge Navigator (concept video, 1987; produced by The Kenwood Group). Internet Archive.

speculations.text: I know kung fu.
speculations.note: Instead of years of training, martial arts are downloaded directly into Neo’s brain: learning without teaching, school or study.
speculations.speaker: Writer or artist
speculations.source: Lana and Lilly Wachowski (dirs), The Matrix (Warner Bros., 1999).

speculations.text: Vulcan children learn alone in individual learning pods, answering a computer’s rapid-fire questions; one asks the young Spock about a twentieth-century Earth song.
speculations.speaker: Writer or artist
speculations.source: J. J. Abrams (dir.), Star Trek (Paramount, 2009).
speculations.verify: Scene described from secondary sources; check against the film.

speculations.who: Corning, A Day Made of Glass 2
speculations.text: Glass surfaces become connected displays throughout a family’s day, including an interactive virtual blackboard at school.
speculations.note: Corporate concept video promoting display glass; later used by teachers as a classroom writing prompt.
speculations.speaker: Company
speculations.source: Corning Incorporated, A Day Made of Glass 2 (concept video, February 2012); reported in IndustryWeek, 21 March 2012.
